NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a demand defrost system using evaporator inlet air temperature hysteresis to trigger defrost only when frost buildup is detected. Standard practice uses a fixed 6-hour interval, regardless of frost level. This is a departure from fixed-timer defrost and differs from simple pressure-based demand defrost (which requires pressure transmitters not permitted by the constraint). The mechanism attacks the failure's driving physics by measuring the temperature rise across the evaporator coil, which correlates directly with frost-induced airflow restriction, and only initiates defrost when restriction crosses a threshold.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is ΔT = T_inlet - T_evap, where a rising ΔT indicates airflow restriction from frost buildup. The mechanism triggers defrost when ΔT exceeds a setpoint (e.g., 5°C above baseline), and waits until ΔT falls below a lower hysteresis band (e.g., 2°C above baseline) before allowing the next trigger. This reduces energy waste by eliminating unnecessary defrosts on clean coils and prevents capacity starvation by ensuring defrost occurs before airflow becomes critically restricted. Magnitude verification: A 5°C ΔT threshold corresponds to approximately 20-30% airflow reduction (typical for industrial evaporators), ensuring intervention occurs before efficiency drops below acceptable levels.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
- (b) Commercial NTC temperature probe, 10kΩ, ±0.5°C, installed at evaporator inlet (replaces existing fixed-timer logic)
- (c) Hysteresis controller setpoints: trigger at 5°C above baseline ΔT, reset at 2°C above baseline ΔT (uses existing control system)
- (c) Defrost duration retuned to 20 min (from 30 min) as frost is now removed proactively (uses existing timer logic)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Standard practice: 4 defrosts/24h × 30 min = 120 min/day defrost time
- Proposed: 2-3 defrosts/24h × 20 min = 40-60 min/day defrost time (operational loss: 0, as defrost occurs during production)
- Hardware: 1 temperature probe (b) vs. standard practice uses no additional hardware (parity in procurement class)
- Commissioning: Parameter setup (c) vs. standard practice uses interval retuning (same class)
- Maintenance: No additional burden (probe same class as existing sensors)
- Operational cost: Energy savings from 60-80 min/day reduced defrost time (≈15-20% energy reduction)

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
Protocol: Monitor ΔT across evaporator coil over 72 hours with standard loading. Record defrost events and energy consumption.
Instruments: Existing temperature sensors, existing energy meter.
Pass/fail: ΔT threshold must trigger defrost within ±10 min of manual verification of frost buildup; energy consumption must be <90% of standard practice baseline over 72 hours.
Duration: 72 hours (3 standard defrost cycles).
Kill criterion: If ΔT exceeds 8°C without triggering defrost, or if energy consumption >95% of baseline, test fails.

MECHANISM CLASS: thermal-hysteresis demand defrost
